pages.note: New page, written from a sandbox session against published extension@4.1.15 with bun 1.2.13 and node 24.18.1. Verified by running: `bunx extension@4.1.15 create my-ext --template=content` scaffolds and prints Bun-named next steps (`2. bun install`, `3. bun dev`), the generated package.json carries `"packageManager": "bun@1.2.13"`, `bun install` writes bun.lock and installs 335 packages, `bun run build` compiles and emits dist/chromium with manifest.json plus content_scripts/content-0.js, and plain `bunx extension@4.1.15 --version` prints 4.1.15 because the bin shebang keeps the process on node. The runtime boundary was verified the same way: `bunx --bun extension@4.1.15 --version` exits with `[Extension.js] Requires Node.js >= 22.12 (you are on 22.6.0). Upgrade Node.js to run the extension CLI.`, which is the guard reading the Node compatibility version that Bun reports, not an installed Node. Read from source rather than run: the detection order in programs/develop/lib/package-manager.ts, the SUPPORTED_PACKAGE_MANAGERS list ['npm','pnpm','yarn','bun','deno'] in programs/develop/lib/constants.ts, the `--ignore-scripts` flag on the automatic install in programs/develop/lib/ensure-develop-artifacts.ts, the `"engines": {"node": ">=22.12"}` field on all four published packages, and TEMPLATE_LOCKFILE_NAMES in programs/create/steps/import-external-template.ts which strips bun.lock and bun.lockb from imported templates. The page deliberately documents no flag for turning the automatic install off: `--install` is registered but marked `[internal]` in the CLI help, and the negated form was not exercised. One product observation, not a page defect, worth filing separately: under `bunx --bun` the guard reports `you are on 22.6.0`, which reads as a stale Node install rather than as the Bun compatibility shim, and gives the reader no hint that the fix is to drop `--bun`.

New page, verified in a sandbox on extension@4.1.15 using a plain JavaScript project scaffolded from the `content` template, with no typescript dependency installed. Verified by running, each case a fresh `rm -rf dist` plus build with a marker string grepped out of dist/chromium/content_scripts/content-0.js: a tsconfig.json with `baseUrl: "."` and `paths: {"@lib/*": ["src/lib/*"]}` resolves `import {BADGE_TEXT} from "@lib/badge.js"`; the same paths block without baseUrl, written as `["./src/lib/*"]`, also resolves; renaming that file to jsconfig.json breaks the build with `Module not found: Can't resolve '@lib/badge.js' in .../src/content`, which is the exact string the page quotes; and a `resolve.alias` set through the `config` hook in extension.config.js resolves the same import. The JavaScript-project claim is the same run, so it is verified rather than assumed. Read from source rather than run: the resolve block in programs/develop/rspack-config.ts lines 483-528 confirms there is no `alias` key and therefore no built-in folder alias, and supplies the `extensions` and `extensionAlias` lists the page prints; the per-framework alias maps in programs/develop/plugin-js-frameworks/js-tools/*.ts supply the table of aliased specifiers; the tsconfig handoff is `compiler.options.resolve.tsConfig = {configFile: tsConfigPath}` in programs/develop/plugin-js-frameworks/index.ts. Two precedence claims were read, not run, and are stated narrowly for that reason: that user aliases beat framework aliases because JsFrameworksPlugin spreads `...compiler.options.resolve.alias` last, and that `webextension-polyfill$` beats a user alias on that exact key because PolyfillPlugin spreads the existing alias first.

New page, almost entirely verified by running against extension@4.1.15. Scaffolded `extension create ts-ext --template=content-typescript`, which emitted a checked-in extension-env.d.ts whose head is exactly the two lines the page quotes, `/// <reference types="extension/types" />` and `/// <reference types="extension/types/polyfill" />`, followed by the wildcard module declarations for css, module.css, png, svg and the rest. `npm install` then `npx tsc --noEmit` failed with 11 errors, including the two the page quotes verbatim: `src/background.ts(19,1): error TS2304: Cannot find name 'chrome'.` and `src/content/scripts.ts(87,30): error TS2503: Cannot find namespace 'chrome'.`. `npm install -D @types/chrome` installed 0.2.9 and the same `npx tsc --noEmit` then produced no output at all. The build was green both before and after, which is the page's point about SWC never reading types. The cause was traced to node_modules/extension/types/index.d.ts line 4, `/// <reference types="chrome" />`, with the package exports map confirming `"./types"` and `"./types/polyfill"` are types-only entries. The scaffolded tsconfig.json really does carry `"include": ["./", "extension-env.d.ts"]`. Read rather than run: the claim that a tsconfig.json which Extension.js generates for a project that has none carries no `include` array comes from defaultTypeScriptConfig in programs/develop/plugin-js-frameworks/js-tools/typescript.ts, and the consequence stated on the page follows from TypeScript's own default of including every file under the containing directory. This page exists because of a product defect that should be filed separately: every TypeScript template fails `tsc --noEmit` out of the box. 32 example projects carry a tsconfig.json and 0 of them declare @types/chrome, because the examples monorepo hoists `"@types/chrome": "^0.0.287"` in its root package.json, which a single scaffolded template never receives.

New page, verified in a sandbox with @biomejs/biome 2.5.12 installed into a project scaffolded from the `content` template on extension@4.1.15. Verified by running: `biome --version` reports 2.5.12; `biome --help` lists check, lint, format, ci, init and migrate, so every command the page prints exists; `biome init` writes a biome.json whose `files.includes` really is `["**", "!!**/dist"]` and whose `vcs` block really is `{enabled: true, clientKind: "git", useIgnoreFile: true}`, both quoted on the page from that output; and `biome check` runs against the project, reports `Checked 13 files in 30ms` and 13 formatting errors, so the setup is functional rather than merely plausible. The inertness claim is the important one and it was measured, not assumed: with biome.json present at the project root, `bun run build` compiled normally, dist/chromium contained only assets, background, content_scripts, images, manifest.json and options, and `find dist -name biome.json` returned nothing. Read from source rather than run: the closed set of root files the build actually discovers (extension.config.js and its variants, the postcss and tailwind configs, tsconfig.json, the .env family), the absence of any biome.json handling anywhere in programs/, the absence of a config-biome entry in programs/extension/helpers/template-catalog.ts, and the `--zip-source` behaviour in programs/develop/plugin-compilation/zip.ts, whose getFilesToZip is an allow-everything-minus-denylist so a root biome.json does land in the source archive. Two claims are named here rather than asserted from a run: `biome migrate eslint --write` and `biome migrate prettier --write` were confirmed to exist in the help output but were not executed against a real ESLint or Prettier config, and the --zip-source packaging detail was read from the zip source rather than produced.

New page. Verified by running against extension@4.1.15: the `content` template scaffolds a content script whose default export is exactly the pattern the page teaches, creating a div, setting `data-extension-root`, applying `all: initial !important`, calling `attachShadow({mode: 'open'})`, and returning a cleanup that removes the host; a production `bun run build` of that project emits a content bundle containing the literal `data:text/css;charset=utf-8,`, which is the inlining the page describes for CSS a content script imports; and the same emitted bundle contains the host selector strings `[data-extension-root]` and `[data-extension-root]:not([data-extension-root=`, confirming both the attribute contract and the reserved `extension-js-devtools` exclusion. Read from source rather than exercised in a live browser: the mount and cleanup wrapper in programs/develop/plugin-web-extension/feature-scripts/steps/add-content-script-wrapper/content-script-wrapper.ts, which supplies the `data-extjs-reinject-owner`, `data-extjs-reinject-key`, `data-extjs-reinject-build` and `data-extjs-reinject-status` attributes with their four status values, the ownership token qualified by extension id, the per-file reinject keys that keep one entry's cleanup off a sibling's host, and the bundle CSS hydration that inserts `<style data-extjs-bundle-css="true">` as the first child and then removes it again when the root already holds a non-empty style of the author's own. The reload sequence the page lists in four steps, and the claim that dev-only attributes are absent from production builds, were both read from that file and from producer-runtime.ts rather than observed in a running page, because this lane launches no headful browser. The manifest CSS claim, that `content_scripts[].css` is injected by the browser into the page document and never reaches a shadow root, is platform behaviour and was not re-derived. The template list is the Content scripts group of programs/extension/helpers/template-catalog.ts.

New page. The central claim was measured directly on extension@4.1.15. A project whose src/manifest.json declares `"permissions": ["storage"]` produced dist/chromium/manifest.json with `["storage"]` after `extension build`, and with `["scripting","tabs","management","storage"]` plus `host_permissions: ["<all_urls>"]` after `extension dev --no-browser`. Both JSON values on the page are copied from those two builds. The warning behaviour was measured in the same way and is the reason the page carries a bolded caveat: appending `chrome.tabs.query({}, () => {})` and `chrome.management.getSelf(() => {})` to the same background.js produced exactly one build warning, for management, quoted verbatim on the page, and none for tabs. Read from source rather than run: INJECTED_PERMISSION_APIS in programs/develop/plugin-web-extension/feature-manifest/steps/apply-dev-defaults.ts is ['storage','scripting','management'] for manifest v3, which is why tabs has no warning, and the manifest v2 injection list is ['tabs','storage'] plus the content script match patterns. The CLI targeting section was read from programs/extension/commands/act.ts and from the control bridge rather than driven against a live browser, because this lane launches no headful browser: `--tab` is a bare `Number()` coercion so it takes an id and nothing else, `--url` is matched first as a tabs.query pattern and then as a substring scan, `--list-tabs` returns id, url, title, active and windowId, `extension storage` registers no `--tab` at all, and `logs --tab` is a post-hoc filter over recorded events rather than a target. The four failure messages in the table are quoted from producer-runtime.ts. Command shapes were checked against the existing command pages so the expression really does precede the options on `extension eval`. The permission table rows about activeTab and about which fields need `tabs` are platform behaviour and were not re-derived. The tabs warning blind spot is a product defect and should be filed separately: an extension that calls chrome.tabs without declaring the permission builds clean, runs clean in dev, and breaks once packaged.

New page. The two Extension.js-specific claims were both measured on extension@4.1.15, and one of them corrected the page during review. The dev server header was verified live: with `extension dev --no-browser` running, ready.json reported port 8080 on host 127.0.0.1, and `curl -D - http://127.0.0.1:8080/...` returned `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` in the response headers. The CSP claim was wrong in the first draft and was rewritten against two observed builds. A project with no `content_security_policy` in its source manifest emits `"script-src 'self'; object-src 'self'; "` in the dev manifest, with no connect-src at all, because manifest v3 leaves connect-src unrestricted unless the author sets it. Adding `"connect-src 'self'"` to the source manifest and running dev again emitted `"script-src 'self'; object-src 'self'; connect-src 'self' ws://127.0.0.1:* ws://localhost:* http://127.0.0.1:* http://localhost:*; "`. Both JSON blocks on the page are copied from those runs, and the page now states the patch as conditional rather than universal. Read from source rather than run: the `headers: {'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*'}` and `allowedHosts: 'all'` settings in programs/develop/dev-server/index.ts and in the HMRDevServer fork, the resolveConnectableHost rule in programs/develop/dev-server/connectable-host.ts that makes a wildcard bind host fall back to 127.0.0.1, and the descriptions of `--host` and `--public-host` registered in programs/extension/commands/dev.ts. The `--host` and `--public-host` example commands were not executed. The claim that Extension.js performs no validation of host_permissions against the URLs in your code is a negative and rests on the absence of any such check in the manifest feature, not on a run. Everything in the context table, the background-fetch pattern, the preflight section and the symptom table is platform behaviour rather than Extension.js behaviour, and was not re-derived here. The E_REMOTE_RESOURCE_BLOCKED wording quoted for remote scripts comes from the error code table in the engine, not from an observed build.
